        step = "step1-trial"
    models = sorted({(e.get("message") or {}).get("model") for e in entries if e.get("type") == "assistant"} - {None, "<synthetic>"})
    slugs = {AGENTS.get(m, "unknown") for m in models}
    slug = slugs.pop() if len(slugs) == 1 else "mixed"
    times = [e["timestamp"] for e in entries if e.get("timestamp")]
    start = usage.parse_time(times[0]).astimezone()
    version = next((e["version"] for e in entries if e.get("version")), "")

    # 1-2. transcript and output snapshot
    run_dir = LOGS / "runs" / f"{step}_{slug}_{session}"

    for f in (REPO / "CLAUDE.md", REPO / "scripts/claude/check.py", ROOT / "references/template.csv", ROOT / "references/metadata.csv"):
        if not (run_dir / f.name).exists():  # first logging of the session = closest to the run
            shutil.copy2(f, run_dir / f.name)

    # 3. sessions.csv line
    sessions = LOGS / "sessions.csv"
    if not sessions.exists():
        with open(sessions, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:

        with open(sessions, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:

    # 4. token columns (only for a known agent, whose log the step wrote)
    if slug in AGENTS.values():
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(Path(usage.__file__)), "--step", "step0" if step == "step0" else "step1",

    outputs = ([LOGS / "md_opt_log.csv", LOGS / "md_opt_check.csv"] if step == "step0" else

    print(f"logged {step} | {slug} | session {session} | {run_dir.relative_to(REPO)}", file=sys.stderr)

lines: +# Data extraction pipeline
+## Setup
+```python
+AGENTS   = {"opus-5-5": "claude-opus-5-5", "sonnet-5-5": "claude-sonnet-5-5"}   # slug: exact model ID; one session per agent
+slug     = AGENTS key whose model ID is the model running this session   # not in AGENTS: stop and tell the user
+MD_AGENT = "opus-5-5"                            # only this agent runs Step 0
+RUN      = "test"                                # "test" = trial run; "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise
+ROOT     = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN]   # read references and write results only under ROOT
+TEMPLATE = ROOT + "references/template.csv"      # row 1 = header (29 columns); rows 2+ = worked examples; new columns = NA in examples
+METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv"      # trait definitions
+MD_RAW   = "data/papers_test/md/*.md"            # pdf2md.py output
+PDF_DONE = "data/papers_test/pdf_done/*.pdf"     # source PDF for each MD_RAW file; same file stem
+MD_OPT   = "data/papers_test/md_agents/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper
+PAPERS   = "data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md"     # extraction input = MD_OPT; pages split by <!-- PAGE BREAK -->
+RESULT   = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv"           # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (27 columns)
+LOG      = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv"          # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS
+MD_LOG   = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv"          # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS
+TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens"   # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them
+USAGE    = "scripts/claude/usage.py"             # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents
+CHECK    = "scripts/claude/check.py"             # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/"
+## Read and write scope
+| Step | Read | Write |
+| 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_agents/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report |
+| 1 | `METADATA`, `TEMPLATE`, `PAPERS` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report |

+Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript.
+## Steps

+`print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`.
+```python
+# Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0.
+print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers")
+if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS)
+for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1):
+    out = MD_OPT(stem(md))
+    if exists(out) and out ends with "<!-- md_opt:":    # finished earlier; resume safe
+        print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | skipped: already done"); continue
+    if exists(out): overwrite(out, "")           # unfinished file from an interrupted run: restart from page 1; status "restarted" in note
+    started = now_utc()
+    pdf = PDF_DONE matching stem(md)
+    if not pdf:                                  # copy md unchanged, add end comment with note
+        copy(md, out); append(out, "<!-- md_opt: ...; note=no matching PDF -->"); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF")
+        print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: copied unchanged"); continue
+    print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages")
+    for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10):       # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once
+        raw = text in md for the same pages      # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers
+        append(out, optimise(raw, batch))        # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches
+        print(f"    pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}")
+    append(out, "<!-- md_opt: model=...; date=YYYY-MM-DD; md_sha256=...; pdf_sha256=...; pdf_pages=N; fixes=...; unresolved=... -->")
+    log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note)   # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas
+    print(f"    done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}")
+run(f"python {CHECK} --step0")                  # see Checks
+print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_skipped} skipped")
+# Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently.
+if any MD_RAW file has no finished MD_OPT file: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first
+print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers")
+if not exists(RESULT):
+    write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS])   # header only; do not copy example rows
+    write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS)
+log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...")   # 1 line per run
+read(METADATA); read(TEMPLATE, rows=2..6 + first 3 rows with PJP mths filled)   # definitions + value format; TEMPLATE column order differs
+for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1):
+    if paper in LOG:                         # finished in an earlier run
+        print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue
+    started = now_utc()
+    remove rows of paper from RESULT         # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by File_name); state count in LOG note
+    if broken(paper):                        # see Broken papers
+        append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason)
+        print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue
+    print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages")
+    for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once
+        append(RESULT, extract(batch))       # write after every batch
+        print(f"    pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}")
+    if n_rows == 0:                          # readable, but no relevant data
+        append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason)
+        print(f"    no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue
+    log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems)
+    print(f"    done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}")
+    check_paper(paper)
+print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers")
+run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}")                # see Checks
+print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed}")

+Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output.

+Token usage: do not estimate tokens. Every log line ends with 6 empty `TOKEN_COLS` cells. After the session, `USAGE` fills them per paper from the session transcript, using the `started` and `finished` times, so record both for every paper.
+## Markdown optimisation
+Compare each `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF.

+- Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown.
+- Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order.
+- Remove conversion junk: `<span id=...>` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers.
+- Put exactly one `<!-- PAGE BREAK -->` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none).
+- Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF.
+- Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`.
+## Extraction rules
+- One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows.
+- Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates.
+- Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty.
+- Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row.
+- Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch.

+- Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire.
+- Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `Location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `Notes`.
+- Site names: use the name as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section; map table codes (e.g. column `A`) to that name. Same site = same string on every row.
+- A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `Notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own.

+- Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `Location_name` = those site names joined by ` / `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites.

+- Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry; `Notes` of each starts with `separate entry in paper` and names what differs.

+- Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `Notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates).

+- Measure defined as a percentage of a cohort or population flowering: 50% -> `Time to 50% flowering`, 80% -> `Time to 80% flowering`, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period).
+- `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` only for: maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed; or the primary-juvenile-period-in-months rule under Time columns.
+- Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N`, e.g. `>4`.

+- Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `Notes`.
+- Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them.
+- Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `Notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `Notes`.
+- Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `Notes` only.

+- Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `Notes`.
+## Broken papers and papers without data
+Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. Write an NA row when:
+- **broken**: file empty or under 1,000 bytes; no `<!-- md_opt:` end comment; end comment lists an `unresolved` table that holds species values; text garbled or unreadable; read error.
+- **no_data**: paper readable, all pages read, no species-level juvenile period or fire response values found.
+```python
+na_row = {name: "NA" for name, rule in COLUMNS}  # exactly 1 NA row per paper
+na_row["Notes"]  = reason                        # e.g. "empty markdown: PDF conversion failed"; "no data: review paper, no species values"
+na_row["Source"] = citation if readable else stem(paper)
+na_row["File_name"] = stem(paper)
+Paper breaks partway: keep rows already extracted, add the 1 NA row, continue with next paper.
+## Columns
+Order in `RESULT`, grouped by similarity. Names match `TEMPLATE` exactly. Columns marked `new` are NA in `TEMPLATE` examples; fill them in `RESULT` when stated.
+```python
+COLUMNS = [
+  # taxon
+  ("Genus", "as printed in paper"),
+  ("Species", "as printed in paper"),
+  ("subsp", "subspecies or variety name; '*' if species introduced / exotic / weed"),
+  ("scientific_name", "Genus + ' ' + Species (+ ' *' if introduced)"),
+  ("Family", "as printed; empty if not stated"),
+  # fire response

+  ("fire_response categorical_surv1", "code defined in paper as killed / fire-sensitive / obligate seeder -> obligate; defined as resprouter -> resprouter; any other code (undefined, minority, mixed, uncertain such as '?r', 'K/r') -> copied exactly as printed, including '?'"),
+  ("resprouter_type", "e.g. basal, epicormic, lignotuber; as printed"),
+  # time after fire: value as printed; range as 'min-max', e.g. 3.0-4.0; see Time columns
+  ("PJP mths", "primary juvenile period, paper reports it in months"),
+  ("primary_juvenile_period", "primary juvenile period, paper reports it in years"),
+  ("Age at first flower production from seed_repr3", "years; time or age to first flowering from seed, other wording"),
+  ("secondary_juvenile_period", "paper's term is 'secondary juvenile period'"),
+  ("Time to first flower production resprout_repr3a", "years; time to first flowering or reproduction of resprouts, other wording"),
+  ("Time to 50% flowering_repr4", "years; maturation age: time for 50% of an even-aged cohort to produce first viable seed; 50% flowering goes to Time to 50% flowering"),
+  ("Time to 50% flowering", "new; time until 50% of individuals flower, as stated in paper; not maturation age"),
+  ("Time to 80% flowering", "new; time until 80% of individuals flower"),
+  ("Recovery_time", "new; time from fire until recovery as defined in paper; recovery measure in Notes, e.g. 'pre-fire cover'"),
+  ("Time_unit", "new; days | weeks | months | years; unit of secondary_juvenile_period, Time to 50% flowering, Time to 80% flowering, Recovery_time; empty if none filled"),
+  # site
+  ("Location_name", "new; study site name as printed; fill only if Latitude and Longitude both empty, or several sites share one set of coordinates"),
+  ("Latitude", "decimal degrees, WGS84; south negative; 33° 45' S -> -33.75"),
+  ("Longitude", "decimal degrees, WGS84; east positive"),
+  ("Rainfall_mm", "rainfall of location, mm; mean annual if stated; other period (e.g. post-fire year) -> period in Notes"),
+  # fire
+  ("Fire_type", "new; wildfire | prescribed burn | experimental burn | as printed"),
+  ("Fire_season_categorical", "Summer | Autumn | Winter | Spring; several seasons joined by '/', e.g. Autumn/Spring; derive from fire date if only date given, note in Notes"),
+  ("Fire_severity_categorical", "Low | Moderate | Moderate-High | High; other scale -> as printed"),
+  # record
+  ("Notes", "assumptions, ambiguities, page number of source table"),
+  ("Source", "full citation of the paper, same string on every row of that paper"),
+  ("File_name", "new; file stem of the paper in PAPERS, e.g. 'Kubiak Cunn 2009'; same on every row of that paper"),
+Time columns:
+- Fixed units: `PJP mths` = months; `primary_juvenile_period`, `_repr3`, `_repr3a`, `_repr4` = years. All other time columns: paper's unit (days, weeks, months or years), recorded in `Time_unit`.
+- Primary juvenile period in months: fill `PJP mths` (months) and `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` (years, no `Notes` entry). In years: fill `primary_juvenile_period` only.

+- Fixed-unit column, value reported in another unit: convert to the column's unit (years = months / 12 = weeks / 52 = days / 365; months = weeks / 4.33 = days / 30.4); write `<column> converted from N <unit>` in `Notes`. No other conversion.
+- Paper gives values under different terms (e.g. age at first flowering and primary juvenile period): each value in its own column. Apart from the months rule above, one value never fills 2 columns.

+- Precision: copy values with exactly the decimals printed in the paper. Do not round or add trailing zeros (`3.0` stays `3.0`; `3` stays `3`). Converted value: paper or source states the value in the target unit -> copy it as printed. Otherwise round to 3 decimals, drop trailing zeros (26 months -> 2.167; 30 months -> 2.5; 48 months -> 4).
+- Ranges: `min-max`, no spaces (`3.0 - 16.0` -> `3.0-16.0`). Open bounds as printed (`>23`, `<2`). Uncertain value: no `?` in the cell; explain in `Notes`.
+- Variable-unit columns in one row use different units: `Time_unit` = unit of most values; list each exception in `Notes`, e.g. `Recovery_time in years`.
+- Omit the 2 unnamed `TEMPLATE` columns (20 and 21). All 27 named columns stay in `RESULT`.

+CSV format: UTF-8, comma separator, LF line endings, decimal point `.`. Quote any cell containing a comma, quote, or newline; double inner quotes. Empty cell = no value; `NA` only in NA rows. Trim leading and trailing spaces in every cell (`TEMPLATE` has some; do not copy them).
+## Checks

+`CHECK` tests every rule that needs no reading of the paper: header and column count, spaces, NA rows, `scientific_name`, coordinates, `Location_name`, time formats, decimals, `Time_unit`, `PJP mths` / 12 = repr4, fire season, rainfall, duplicates, `LOG` lines and row counts. It prints a summary, writes a report to `ROOT + "logs/"`, and exits 1 if any check fails.
+```python
+def check_paper(paper):                          # after every paper's LOG line, including broken and no_data; never skip
+    for attempt in 1..3:
+        if run(f"python {CHECK} {slug} --paper '{stem(paper)}'") == 0: return
+        fix each failed row from the paper; fix LOG n_rows if rows changed
+    log the remaining errors in the paper's LOG note

+After all papers: run `CHECK` without `--paper`, fix errors the same way. After Step 0: run `CHECK --step0`, fix each failed `MD_OPT` file from its PDF. Warnings: look, fix if real. Never delete a row silently.
+## Do not
+- Read `data/reference/` or another agent's `RESULT` or `LOG`. They contain answers.
+- Edit `TEMPLATE`, `METADATA`, `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE`, or anything in `data/papers_test/` outside `md_agents/`.
+- Copy example rows from `TEMPLATE` into `RESULT`.
+- Edit `CHECK`, or write any script file outside the session scratchpad.
+- Create or write anything in `data/inference/`. Use `data/inference_test/` only.
+"""Check extraction output against the rules in CLAUDE.md.

+Only checks that need no reading of the paper. Never edits RESULT or LOG.
+Writes a report to data/inference_test/logs/{slug}_check.csv (or md_opt_check.csv)
+and exits 1 if any check fails.
+import argparse

+MD_LOG_HEADER = ["paper", "status", "pdf_pages", "n_tables", "n_fixes", "unresolved", "started", "finished", "note"] + TOKEN_COLS
+STATUSES = {"done", "broken", "no_data"}
+FIXED_YEARS = [
+    "Age at first flower production from seed_repr3",

+NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"-?\d+(\.\d+)?")

+def columns_from_claude_md():
+    """Read the COLUMNS list from CLAUDE.md so both files share one definition."""
+    text = (REPO / "CLAUDE.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    block = text[text.index("COLUMNS = ["):]
+    block = block[:block.index("\n]")]

+class Report:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.items = []
+    def error(self, where, column, check, value=""):
+        self.items.append(("error", where, column, check, value))
+    def warn(self, where, column, check, value=""):
+        self.items.append(("warning", where, column, check, value))
+    def n(self, level):
+        return sum(1 for item in self.items if item[0] == level)
+    def write(self, path):
+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:

for f in sorted(o.File_name.unique()):
    a=o[o.File_name==f].reset_index(drop=True); b=s[s.File_name==f].reset_index(drop=True)

    print(f"\n== {f}: rows {len(a)} vs {len(b)}")
    if d is None: continue
    rows=d.any(axis=1).sum()
    print("  rows differing (excl Notes):",rows, "| Notes differ:",(a.Notes!=b.Notes).sum())
    cc=d.sum(); print("  "+", ".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k,v in cc[cc>0].items()))
    # multiset compare ignoring order
    ka=a[cols].apply(tuple,axis=1).value_counts(); kb=b[cols].apply(tuple,axis=1).value_counts()
    diff=(ka.sub(kb,fill_value=0)!=0).sum()

content.text:
The two models agree on almost all the extracted values. Most of the differences are in how they write names, sites and citations. The real content differences are in 2 papers: Ooi and Kubiak.

**Overall**
- Both have 4124 rows. Row counts match per paper (65, 33, 1306, 8, 13, 2699).
- Both pass the checks with 0 errors. Warnings: opus 6, sonnet 4.
- Tokens: opus used 7.36M tokens over 47 requests (about 9 min). Sonnet used 6.05M over 43 requests (about 7 min).

**Values (fire response and time columns), matched by taxon**
- Benson, Knox & Clarke, Muir: identical.
- nswfrrd: identical values. Only the taxon matching differs (see below).
- Kubiak: 2 fire response codes differ. Opus keeps the annotation printed after the code (`R(1)m.i.f`, `K;r–m.i.f71w`); sonnet cuts it (`R(1)`, `K;r`). Opus also keeps the printed spacing (`? r`, `K/ r`); sonnet removes it.
- Ooi, *Leucopogon exolasius*, Dingo site, summer fire:
  - Opus fills 9.97 (50%) and 11.51 (80%) from the text, and also the pooled table value 9.96 on the shared-site row.
  - Sonnet fills only the pooled 9.96, but does fill the Dingo winter value (11.35), so it treats the two fires differently.
  - The rule ("several estimates: main table value, others in Notes") is unclear here. The Dingo row and the shared row are different site rows.

**Systematic differences in form**
- **`subsp`:** opus writes the bare name (`buxifolia`). Sonnet writes the prefix too (`subsp. buxifolia`, `var. lanceolatus`) and adds it to `scientific_name`. Opus leaves the subspecies out of `scientific_name`. This affects about 330 rows.
- **Species names:** sonnet keeps `(s.lat.)` in `Species`; opus drops it. In nswfrrd, opus keeps `subsp X` inside `Species` in about 15 rows.
- **Exotic `*`:** opus marks 511 rows, sonnet 491. When a taxon is both a subspecies and exotic, opus writes `*` and drops the subspecies (e.g. *Chrysanthemoides monilifera*). Sonnet keeps the subspecies and drops `*`. The column can't hold both.
- **`Source`:** opus uses `Benson, D. H. (1985). …`; sonnet uses `Benson DH (1985) …`. Each model is consistent within a paper. Sonnet's Knox page range (`348-353`) looks more complete than opus's, but I did not check it against the paper.
- **`Location_name`:**
  - Benson: opus `Site A`; sonnet `Brisbane Water National Park site A`.
  - Ooi: opus `Site 1 – Dingo`; sonnet `Dingo`.
  - Knox: the two models write fire season as `Autumn/Spring` and `Spring/Autumn`.

**Kubiak sites**
- The paper gives coordinates only for the Lane Cove River valley (and the same coordinates in the abstract for "northern Sydney"). Narrabeen is described as 15 km to the northeast, with no coordinates.
- Opus leaves Narrabeen's coordinates empty and puts no name on the Lane Cove rows.
- Sonnet gives Narrabeen the Lane Cove coordinates and names both sites. Opus's reading is more defensible.

**Rules unclear (both models disagree within the rules):**
- `subsp` format, and how to mark a taxon that is both a subspecies and exotic.
- Citation style for `Source`.
- Whether to keep annotations after a fire response code.
- Site-specific value given in the text versus the pooled table value.
- Whether site names should include the park or site label.

`Notes` differ on every row, as expected for free text. I did not compare them in detail.

content.text:
I've updated the 4 rules in `CLAUDE.md`. Nothing is committed.

1. **Subspecies:** `subsp` now holds the name without the word "subsp." (`subsp. buxifolia` becomes `buxifolia`). I also changed `Species` to hold only the species epithet, with the subspecies or variety name going in `subsp`. Without that, rows like nswfrrd's `oleifolius subsp canescens` would still have the subspecies inside `Species`.
2. **Family:** written as printed, with only the first letter capitalised (`MYRTACEAE` becomes `Myrtaceae`).
3. **Source:** full citation in APA style. The rule includes the Benson 1985 citation as an example.
4. **Site names:** copied exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section, with no words added or removed. Table codes (e.g. column `A`) still map to that name.

**Decisions for you:**
- **`var.`:** you said to remove "subsp", so I kept "var." and "f." as printed (`var. lanceolatus`). If you want those words dropped too, I'll change the rule.
- **`scientific_name`:** still Genus + Species + ` *`, with no subspecies. This doesn't change your 4 rules, but opus and sonnet handled it differently. Should the subspecies be added to `scientific_name`?
- **Exotic subspecies:** for a taxon that is both a subspecies and exotic, `subsp` can hold only one of `*` or the name. Opus and sonnet split on this too.
- **`check.py`:** it doesn't test the new rules for Family, subsp or Source. I didn't change it, because `CLAUDE.md` says to leave it fixed.

The new `CLAUDE.md` changes its hash, so both models need to run Step 1 again. Before each re-run, move the current results and logs into `runs/` again; the snapshots there already match them.

content.text:
`var.` means **variety** (Latin *varietas*). It is a botanical rank below species, like `subsp.` (subspecies).

- **Order:** species, then subspecies (`subsp.`), then variety (`var.`), then form (`f.` or `forma`).
- **Example:** *Leucopogon lanceolatus* var. *lanceolatus* is a variety of *L. lanceolatus*.
- **Difference:** a subspecies usually differs more and has its own geographic range. A variety usually differs less, for example in hairiness or leaf shape. In practice authors use the two inconsistently.
- **Why it matters here:** the rank word is part of the name. *Banksia spinulosa* var. *cunninghamii* is not the same name as *B. spinulosa* subsp. *cunninghamii*. If `subsp` holds only `cunninghamii`, the rank is lost.

You can keep the rank in one of two ways:
1. Drop only `subsp.` and keep `var.` and `f.`. This is the current rule.
2. Drop every rank word and add a `rank` column. That changes the 27-column format.

I recommend option 1. Under it, a bare name in `subsp` means subspecies, and the printed `var.` or `f.` marks the other ranks.

`f.` means **form** (Latin *forma*). It is the lowest common botanical rank, below variety. A form usually marks one small difference, such as flower colour; *Haloragis glauca* f. *glauca* is an example. The nswfrrd paper prints the rank word out as `forma`.

- **Rank words written the same way:** `ssp.` or `subsp` becomes `subsp.`, `variety` becomes `var.`, and `forma` becomes `f.`.
- **Rare ranks** such as `nothosubsp.` (a hybrid subspecies) are kept as printed.
- **`Species`:** holds the epithet only. The rank and name always go in `subsp`.

This replaces your rule 1 ("remove subsp"). Sonnet's last run already wrote `subsp` this way; opus did not.

- **Exotic subspecies:** `subsp` can hold `*` or the rank and name, not both.

content.text:
The `scientific_name` rule in `metadata.csv` now says never to include the subspecies, variety or form, e.g. `Acacia buxifolia` or `Acacia buxifolia *`.

`*` marks a taxon that is **introduced**: exotic, a weed, or not native to the study location. Many Australian floras and papers print `*` before the name, e.g. `*Lantana camara`. The pipeline copies it in two places:
- `subsp` = `*`
- `scientific_name` = `Genus Species *`, e.g. `Lantana camara *`

`check.py` errors if these two don't match.

**The problem:** an exotic taxon with a subspecies needs two things in `subsp`, e.g. `*Chrysanthemoides monilifera` subsp. *monilifera*. Opus kept `*` and lost the subspecies; sonnet kept the subspecies and lost `*`.

**Options:**

content.text:
**Introduced from where?** That depends on the paper, and the papers don't define it.
- **Kubiak 2009:** "576 native species and 252 exotic species" in the abstract, but no reference region is stated.
- **nswfrrd:** marks taxa with an `Exotic` code. NSW appears to be the reference region: *Acacia saligna*, which is native to Western Australia, is marked `Exotic`. So "introduced" there includes plants from other states.
- **Benson, Knox & Clarke, Muir, Ooi:** no marking.

So the rule says: "not native to the study location, as the paper defines it." The region is whatever the paper uses, such as NSW or Australia. Agents must use only the paper's own marking, never background knowledge. Without that limit, agents would have to decide native ranges themselves.

**Option 3 changes:**
- **`metadata.csv`:** new `introduced` row after `scientific_name`. Values: `yes` or empty. It is `yes` when the paper marks the taxon by a symbol (`*`), a code (`Exotic`) or in the text. The paper's term and reference region, when stated, go in `Notes`.
- **`subsp`:** rank and name only, never `*`.
- **`scientific_name`:** Genus + Species only, with no subspecies and no `*`.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** `introduced` added to `COLUMNS`, flagged `new`. The column count is now 28 (27 `TEMPLATE` columns plus `introduced`).

**Checks:** the column names in `CLAUDE.md` and `metadata.csv` match (28 each). `check.py` needs no change, because its `*` check at line 162 still passes when neither column has `*`.

**Your meta-analysis data:** `TEMPLATE` has no `introduced` column, and its rows use `subsp = *`. You'll need to map one format to the other when you merge.

content.text:
I replaced the `introduced` column with `native_status`. It sits after `scientific_name`, and there are still 28 columns.

The rule is in `metadata.csv`:
- **Values:** the paper's own term, in lower case: `native`, `introduced`, `exotic`, `naturalised`, `weed`, or another term as printed.
- **Where the term can come from:** a symbol or code the paper defines (`*` = introduced; nswfrrd's `Exotic` code), a table column, or the text.
- **Unmarked taxa:** `native` only if the paper says unmarked taxa are native. Otherwise the cell stays empty, so agents can't assume.
- **Reference region:** in `Notes` if the paper states it (e.g. NSW, Australia).
- **Paper only:** never background knowledge.

`subsp` now says "never `*`; native or introduced status goes in `native_status`". The column names in `CLAUDE.md` and `metadata.csv` still match.

Expected results in the current papers:
- nswfrrd: `exotic` for taxa with the `Exotic` code.
- Kubiak: `exotic` for marked taxa, if the appendix marks them. Unmarked taxa may get `native`, since the abstract counts 576 native and 252 exotic species. Agents will decide from the appendix legend.
- Benson, Knox & Clarke, Muir, Ooi: empty.

Nothing is committed.

The new rules mostly worked: the models now agree on `Source`, `Family`, `subsp`, `native_status` and site names. 6 disagreements remain: 3 are rules that need clarifying, and 3 look like model errors.

**Runs**
- Both runs used the same `CLAUDE.md` (`0d03c029…`), and both pass the checks with 0 errors and 6 warnings each.
- Rows: opus 4116, sonnet 4122. The 6-row gap is all in Benson.
- Tokens: opus 6.25M over 43 requests; sonnet 4.77M over 35 requests.
- An extra session `e505b693` (15:47) is logged as `step1_mixed`, with no models and no tokens. It was probably started and closed before it ran anything. Its `runs/` folder and `sessions.csv` row can be deleted if you want.

**Now the same in both**
- **`Source`:** identical APA citations.
- **`native_status`:** Kubiak has 298 `exotic`, nswfrrd 213 `exotic`, and all other rows are empty. Unmarked Kubiak taxa stayed empty: the abstract's "576 native" count did not make either model fill `native`.
- **`subsp`:** both use `subsp.` / `var.` and match exactly.
- **`Family`, Benson site names (`Site A`…), Muir, Ooi, nswfrrd:** identical.

**Remaining differences**
1. **Benson:**
   - *Banksia oblongifolia* and *B. serrata* are printed as "no flowering yet" separately for each of the 4 sites. Sonnet wrote 4 rows per species; opus merged them into 1 shared row, which breaks the "never merge rows" rule. **Opus is wrong.**
   - Severity: opus wrote `hot` (the paper's word, allowed by "other scale, as printed"); sonnet left it empty. **Sonnet is wrong.**
2. **Knox:** the paper burned Imbota in spring and Booroolong in autumn, and doesn't say which species grew at which reserve. Opus wrote `Autumn/Spring`; sonnet left it empty and explained in `Notes`. The rule ("several seasons joined by '/'") supports opus.
3. **Kubiak values printed with "buds"** (e.g. `190w–buds`), about 13 taxa. Opus put them in `repr3a`/`repr3` as first flowering; sonnet kept them in `Notes` only, since buds aren't flowers. Sonnet's reading is safer, but the rules don't say.
4. **Kubiak value placement:** for about 6 taxa recorded at both catchments, the models put a time value on different rows. For some (e.g. *Xanthorrhoea*) it went on a single-site row in opus and on the shared row in sonnet; for *Persoonia lanceolata* it was the reverse.
5. **Kubiak fire response codes:** opus copies the printed text exactly (`R(1)m.i.f`, `K;r`, `? r`, `K/ r`). Sonnet translates or tidies it (`resprouter`, `obligate`, `?r`, `K/r`). The rule says to copy undefined and mixed codes exactly, so **sonnet is wrong** on `K;r` and `R(1)m.i.f`.
6. **Kubiak names:** opus keeps the printed marks: `?stenophylla`, `(*?)Acacia`, `subsp. ?subulata`, and an en dash in `bursa–pastoris`. Sonnet strips the `?` and `(*?)` marks and uses a hyphen. The `Notes` page numbers also differ: opus gives journal pages (p. 155) and sonnet gives PDF pages (p. 25).

**Rules to clarify:**
- Do flower buds count as flowering?
- Are `?` and other uncertainty marks in taxon names kept or moved to `Notes`? There is a rule for this in value columns but not in names.
- En dash or hyphen in names?
- Should `Notes` page numbers be journal pages or PDF pages?
- Does "no flowering yet" at every site mean one row per site? The rule already says never merge, but a sentence about this case would help.

Nothing is committed. Do you want me to add these clarifications to the rules?

content.text:
Yes, for rules a script can test without reading the paper. Agents run `check.py` after every paper and fix what it flags, so a rule it tests gets applied the same way by both models. A rule written only in text gets followed less reliably.

**Errors** (safe to test strictly):
- **Dashes:** no `–` or `—` in any cell.
- **`fire_response categorical_surv1`:** no spaces inside the code.
- **`Genus`, `Species`, `subsp`:** none of `?`, `*`, `(` or `)`.
- **`Genus`:** one word, capitalised (`Acacia`).
- **`Species`:** lower case, no rank words.
- **`subsp`:** empty, or a rank (`subsp.`, `var.`, `f.`, `nothosubsp.`) plus a name.
- **`scientific_name`:** exactly `Genus + " " + Species`. This replaces the current `*` check at line 162.
- **`native_status`:** lower case, no `*`.

**Warnings** (heuristic, so agents look but aren't forced):
- **`Family`:** not ALL CAPS. Kubiak's `Fabaceae (Faboideae)` must still pass.
- **`Source`:** looks like APA (`Author, A. B. (YYYY). Title.`). nswfrrd has no citation, so its file-stem `Source` must not fail.
- **`Notes`:** a page reference that is neither `p. N` nor `PDF p. N` (e.g. `page 25`, `pg 25`).

**Not testable:** whether `p. N` is the journal page or the PDF page, and whether a site name is exactly as printed. Both need the paper.

**Caution:** each failed check costs the agent up to 3 fix attempts. A wrong error, such as flagging a real name with a hyphen like `bursa-pastoris`, wastes tokens and can push agents to change correct data. So I'd make only the certain rules errors.

`CLAUDE.md` says never edit `CHECK`, but that rule is for agents during a run. If you approve, I'll make these changes between runs and test them on the current 2 result files before you re-run. Should I go ahead?

content.text:
I've added the format checks to `scripts/claude/check.py`. On the current results they flag only real breaks of the new rules, plus some harmless warnings.

**Errors:**
- **Dashes:** an en or em dash in any cell.
- **`scientific_name`:** must be exactly `Genus + " " + Species`. This replaces the old `*` check.
- **`Genus`, `Species`, `subsp`:** no `?` or `*`.
- **`Genus`:** one capitalised word.
- **`Species`:** no rank words (`subsp`, `var.`, `f.`…).
- **`subsp`:** a rank word plus name. `subsp. A`, `f. B`, `cv. Bulbillifera` and `subsp. prostratum var. prostratum` all pass.
- **`native_status`:** lower case.
- **Fire response codes:** no space next to `?`, `/`, `;`, `,` or a bracket.

**Warnings:**
- **`Species`:** not a plain lower-case epithet. This is a warning because phrase names like `sp. A sensu Harden (1994)` and hybrids like `X crocosmiiflora` are real names.
- **`Family`:** in ALL CAPS.
- **`Source`:** doesn't look like APA. A paper with no citation, whose `Source` is its file stem (nswfrrd), is skipped.
- **`Notes`:** a page reference written as `page N`, `pg N` or `pp N`.

**Code-space rule changed:** nswfrrd separates 2 codes with a space (`R s`, `S R`, about 430 rows). Removing all spaces would turn `R s` into `Rs`. So the rule in `metadata.csv` now removes only spaces next to punctuation (`? r` becomes `?r`) and keeps the space between 2 codes.

**Test on the current results** (written before these rules):

| Dashes in `Notes` | 259 | 541 |

content.text:
Use one separator for every list column, and make sure it never appears inside a single value. Right now the results use `/` for lists, and `/` also appears inside printed values. I recommend switching lists to `; ` (semicolon and space).

**Lists in the current results (opus; sonnet is the same):**

| Column | Separator | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `Location_name` (shared row) | ` / ` | `Site A / Site B` |
| `Fire_season_categorical` | `/` | `Autumn/Spring` |
| `resprouter_type` | `/` | `basal/lignotuber` (26 rows) |

**Where `/` clashes with printed values:**
- **`fire_response categorical_surv1`:** `/` is part of Kubiak's printed codes (`K/r`, `R/k`), which are single codes, not lists.
- **`Location_name`:** one printed name contains `/`. `Dandenong Ranges National Park / Bunyip State Park/Kurth Kiln Regional Park` (8 rows) can't be split cleanly.

**Why `; `:**
- It is rare in names, sites and seasons. Its one printed use is Kubiak's code `K;r`, which is in a column that never holds lists.
- It is easy to split: in R, `tidyr::separate_rows(col, sep = "; ")`; in Excel, Text to Columns with `;`.
- It reads well: `Autumn; Spring`, `Site A; Site B`.

**Alternatives:**
- **`|`:** it never appears in printed text, but it is harder to read, and the markdown input uses `|` for tables, which could confuse agents.
- **One value per row:** the tidiest option for analysis, but it multiplies rows. Your rules already do this for sites and fires; the shared ` / ` row is the exception.

**Rule I'd add:** "Several values in one cell: separate with `; `. A `/` printed inside a value (e.g. a code `K/r`, a site name) stays as printed." Then switch `Fire_season_categorical`, `Location_name` and `resprouter_type` to `; `. `check.py` could also flag ` / ` in those columns.

The rules now use `; ` to separate several values in one cell, and `check.py` flags the old `/` style.

**Changes:**
- **`CLAUDE.md`, CSV format:** several values in one cell are separated with `; `. A `/` printed inside a single value (code `K/r`, a site name) stays as printed.
- **`CLAUDE.md`, shared-site rule:** site names are joined by `; ` instead of ` / `.
- **`metadata.csv`, rules:** `Fire_season_categorical` becomes `Autumn; Spring`, `resprouter_type` becomes `basal; lignotuber`, and `Location_name` on the shared row becomes `Dingo; Lake Eckersley`.
- **`metadata.csv`, examples:** some example cells used `; ` to list several examples, which would now read as one value with 2 parts. Alternatives are now separated by ` | `, the same as in `allowed_values`, and `CLAUDE.md` explains this.
- **`check.py`, season:** a season joined by `/` is now an error, because the season format is strict.
- **`check.py`, sites and resprouting types:** ` / ` in `Location_name`, or any `/` in `resprouter_type`, is a warning, because a printed name can contain `/`.

**Test on the current results:** each model has 34 errors (33 seasons with `/` and the expected `claude_md_sha256` mismatch) and about 377 warnings. Most warnings are the 328 shared-site rows and 26 resprouting types that use `/`. I put the check reports back after the test.

content.text:
Nearly all of the errors and warnings come from the separator rule I added after these runs. The runs themselves passed the checks they ran under: 0 errors, and 30 (opus) or 31 (sonnet) warnings. The counts below are from re-checking those results with the new `check.py`.

Both models produce the same counts, so on these points their format already matches.

**Errors (34 per model):**
- **33 × `Fire_season_categorical`:** `Spring/Autumn` (Knox). The season must now be joined by `; `, as in `Spring; Autumn`. Both models wrote it the old way because the rule didn't exist yet.
- **1 × `claude_md_sha256`:** the hash in the run's LOG is from the old `CLAUDE.md`. This is expected, because I edited `CLAUDE.md` after the runs. The next run fixes it.

**Warnings:**
- **320 × `Location_name`:** shared rows like `Dingo / Lake Eckersley` should become `Dingo; Lake Eckersley`. Old separator again.
- **26 × `resprouter_type`:** `basal/lignotuber` should become `basal; lignotuber`. Old separator again.
- **24 (opus) / 25 (sonnet) × `Species`:** phrase names and hybrids such as `sp.`, `sp. 'Rocky Creek'` and `X crocosmiiflora`. These are real names, and the warning only asks agents to look. Sonnet has 1 more, `(hybrid)`, from Kubiak's `Petunia (hybrid)`.
- **6 × duplicates:** the same taxon printed twice in the paper, marked `separate entry in paper`. The rules allow this.

All errors and the separator warnings will go away in the next run, since agents will follow the new rules. That leaves about 30 warnings that are expected: phrase names and duplicates.

import csv,re
from collections import Counter
R=lambda n:list(csv.DictReader(open(f"data/inference_test/results/{n}.csv",encoding="utf-8")))
o,s=R("opus-5-5"),R("sonnet-5-5")
print("nswfrrd Source O:",{r["Source"] for r in o if r["File_name"].startswith("nsw")}," S:",{r["Source"] for r in s if r["File_name"].startswith("nsw")})
def shape(v):
    v=re.sub(r"[A-Z]","A",v); v=re.sub(r"[a-z]+","a",v); v=re.sub(r"\d+","9",v); return v
skip={"Notes","Source"}
for c in o[0]:
    if c in skip: continue
    a=Counter(shape(r[c]) for r in o); b=Counter(shape(r[c]) for r in s)
    oa=set(a)-set(b); sb=set(b)-set(a)
    if oa or sb: print(f"{c}:\n   O-only shapes {[(k,a[k]) for k in sorted(oa)][:8]}\n   S-only shapes {[(k,b[k]) for k in sorted(sb)][:8]}")
# Notes style
for n,d in (("O",o),("S",s)):
    pages=Counter(m.group(0) for r in d for m in re.finditer(r"\b(PDF p\.|pp?\.|page)\s?\d",r["Notes"]))
    print(n,"Notes page refs:",dict(Counter(re.sub(r"\d","",k) for k in pages.elements())), "| sep styles:",Counter(("; " in r["Notes"]) for r in d))
E

**Runs:**
- Both used the same `CLAUDE.md` (`c5d265ae…`), and both pass `check.py` with 0 errors.
- Opus used 8.03M tokens over 47 requests; sonnet used 7.06M over 46 requests.

**What now matches in format:**
- Separators: `; ` everywhere, with no ` / ` and no `/` between seasons.
- Hyphens instead of en dashes.
- Clean names: no `?` or `*`; `subsp.`/`var.` in `subsp`; `scientific_name` = Genus + Species.
- `Family`, `native_status`, the APA `Source` citations, and the time columns.
- `Notes` page references: `p. N` or `PDF p. N`.

- Opus wrote a description in `Source`: `nswfrrd v1.3a species data [PDF version]. No author, title or date printed…`.
- Sonnet wrote the file stem.

**Content differences (fine for this phase):**
- Kubiak site names: opus wrote `Lane Cove River valley`, sonnet `Lane Cove River catchment area`. Both are names printed in the paper.
- Benson: 59 vs 65 rows. Ooi: 13 vs 5 rows.
- 2 Kubiak fire codes: the models disagree on where a code ends (`K;r-m.i.f` vs `K;r`).

Opus repeats information about the whole paper on every row, such as code definitions and site and fire descriptions. Sonnet writes mostly notes about that row.

**Fixed: item order.** The `Notes` rule in `metadata.csv` now sets one order, with items separated by `; `:
1. `separate entry in paper …`, if it applies. An existing rule already requires this to come first.
2. Where the row's values came from: `Table 2, p. 342` or `Appendix 1, p. 145`.
3. Other notes, each naming its column where it has one, e.g. `Time to first flower production resprout_repr3a converted from 43 weeks`.

**Needs your decision: information about the whole paper.** Code definitions and site and fire descriptions are currently free to go on every row. That is the main reason opus's `Notes` are 2.4 times longer, and it costs output tokens: about 4100 rows × 200 extra characters.

1. **Row-specific only (recommended).** Information about the whole paper goes once in the paper's LOG `note`. This gives short, uniform `Notes` and fewer tokens.
2. **Repeat on every row.** Each row explains itself on its own, which helps if rows are later separated from their paper. It is longer, and you'd want a fixed list of what to repeat.

Which do you want? Nothing is committed.

content.text:
Neither option changes the rows. Rows stay as they are: 1 per species × site × fire, so a species at 2 sites or with 2 fires gets 2 rows. Your idea of 1 species per row per paper is close to that rule. The options only decide what goes in the `Notes` cell of each row.

**Option 1:** a row's `Notes` holds only notes about that species on that row. Paper-wide information is written once in the paper's LOG `note`. Example row:
`Table 2, p. 342; Age at first flower production from seed_repr3 converted from 18 months`

**Option 2:** every row's `Notes` also repeats the paper-wide information. Example row:
`Table 2, p. 342; Age at first flower production from seed_repr3 converted from 18 months; fire response codes: R = majority resprouted, K = majority killed; Lane Cove River valley burnt 6-8 January 1994, high intensity`

Both models passed the checks they ran under, with 0 errors. 4 format differences remained; I've added rules for all 4, and 2 of them are now checked by `check.py`.

**Runs**

| | opus | sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens (requests) | 7.27M (46) | 8.14M (50) |
| Errors at run time | 0 | 0 |
| Warnings | 30 | 35 |
| Errors with the new checks | 0 | 5 |

The warnings are expected: phrase names like `sp. A` and duplicates marked `separate entry in paper`.

**Last round's fixes worked:**
- **`Source` for nswfrrd:** both models now write the file stem.
- **`Notes` order:** almost every row starts with its source location; only 3 opus rows and 1 sonnet row start differently, and all 4 are values from the running text. `Notes` are long (opus 649 characters on average, sonnet 812), as expected now that paper-wide notes go on every row.

**Format differences left, now covered by rules:**
1. **Hyphenated epithets:** sonnet wrote `novae- zelandiae` and `luteo- album`, with a space after the hyphen (3 rows in nswfrrd). The `Species` rule says a hyphenated epithet is one word, and `check.py` now errors on a space next to a hyphen in a name.
2. **`nothosubsp.` in `Species`:** sonnet wrote `glutinosa nothosubsp. luerssenii` (2 rows); opus put the rank in `subsp`. `check.py`'s rank check missed `nothosubsp.` and `nothovar.` and now catches them. Those are the 5 new errors.
3. **DOI in `Source`:** opus added `https://doi.org/…` for Muir and Ooi; sonnet didn't. The rule now says to end with the DOI if the paper prints one, otherwise no DOI or URL.
4. **`Notes` wording:** opus wrote `text, p. 21`, sonnet `Text, p. 21` and sometimes a `Paper-wide:` label. The rule now says `text, p. 21` for values from the running text, and no `Paper-wide:` label.

**Content differences, which are fine:** Benson 66 vs 65 rows, Kubiak 1301 vs 1307, Ooi 5 vs 13. The models also swapped the Kubiak site names this round (`Lane Cove River` vs `Lane Cove River valley`), and severity is free text in places (`hot`, `low to medium intensity`, `Low; Moderate`).

I put the check reports back after testing. Nothing is committed; `metadata.csv` and `check.py` have changed again.

The differences are getting smaller each round. I'd run 1 more round to confirm the DOI rule and the hyphen and `nothosubsp.` checks. If that round is clean, commit and move to the full set.

Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. # Global instructions

Ported from the pi coding agent's default system prompt (pi 0.87.0).

- Be concise in your responses.
- Show file paths clearly when working with files.
- Reply in caveman style (level: ultra) in every chat response, for the whole session. Do not drift back to full sentences in long sessions.
- Keep files, code, comments, commits and docs in normal prose; caveman style applies to chat replies only.

# Data extraction pipeline ## Setup ```python AGENTS = {"opus-5-5": "claude-opus-5-5", "sonnet-5-5": "claude-sonnet-5-5"} # slug: exact model ID; one session per agent slug = AGENTS key whose model ID is the model running this session # not in AGENTS: stop and tell the user MD_AGENT = "opus-5-5" # only this agent runs Step 0 RUN = "test" # "test" = trial run; "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT TEMPLATE = ROOT + "references/template.csv" # row 1 = header (29 columns); rows 2+ = worked examples; new columns = NA in examples METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example; ' | ' separates alternatives in allowed_values and example MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md/*.md" # pdf2md.py output PDF_DONE = "data/papers_test/pdf_done/*.pdf" # source PDF for each MD_RAW file; same file stem MD_OPT = "data/papers_test/md_agents/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md" # extraction input = MD_OPT; pages split by RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (28 columns) LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" ``` ## Read and write scope | Step | Read | Write | |---|---|---| | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_agents/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | | 1 | `METADATA`, `TEMPLATE`, `PAPERS` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. ## Steps `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. ```python # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): out = MD_OPT(stem(md)) if exists(out) and out ends with ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: copied unchanged"); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") append(out, "") log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_skipped} skipped") # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. if any MD_RAW file has no finished MD_OPT file: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") if not exists(RESULT): write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only; do not copy example rows write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run read(METADATA); read(TEMPLATE, rows=2..6 + first 3 rows with PJP mths filled) # column rules + value format; TEMPLATE column order differs for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue started = now_utc() remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by File_name); state count in LOG note if broken(paper): # see Broken papers append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. Token usage: do not estimate tokens. Every log line ends with 6 empty `TOKEN_COLS` cells. After the session, `USAGE` fills them per paper from the session transcript, using the `started` and `finished` times, so record both for every paper. ## Markdown optimisation Compare each `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. ## Extraction rules - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `Location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `Notes`. - Site names: copy the name exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section. Do not add words (e.g. park or region name) and do not remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column `A`) to that name. Same site = same string on every row. - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `Notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `Location_name` = those site names joined by `; `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites. - Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry; `Notes` of each starts with `separate entry in paper` and names what differs. - Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `Notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates). - Measure defined as a percentage of a cohort or population flowering: 50% -> `Time to 50% flowering`, 80% -> `Time to 80% flowering`, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). - `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` only for: maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed; or the primary-juvenile-period-in-months rule under Time columns. - Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N`, e.g. `>4`. - Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `Notes`. - Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them. - Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `Notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `Notes`. - Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `Notes` only. - Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `Notes`. ## Broken papers and papers without data Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. Write an NA row when: - **broken**: file empty or under 1,000 bytes; no `

- [Always log pipeline runs](always-log-pipeline-runs.md) — every Step 0/1 session: snapshot, sessions.csv, tokens via SessionEnd hook
- [Rule refinement goal](rule-refinement-goal.md) — current phase: same output format across models; content differences OK

```markdown
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. # Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family and Haiku 4.5. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 4.5: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
