"full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise 10 ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT 11 TEMPLATE = ROOT + "references/template.csv" # row 1 = header (29 columns); rows 2+ = worked examples; new columns = NA in examples 12 METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example; ' | ' separates alternatives in allowed_values and example 13 MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md/*.md" # pdf2md.py output for scanned PDFs only (text-layer PDFs go straight to md_agents/) 14 PDF_DONE = "data/papers_test/pdf_done/*.pdf" # source PDF for each MD_RAW file; same file stem 15 MD_OPT = "data/papers_test/md_agents/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper 16 PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md" # extraction input: MD_OPT files of scanned PDFs + raw pdf2md files of text-layer PDFs (end comment "md_opt: none"); pages split by 17 RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (28 columns) 18 LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS 19 MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS 20 TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them 21 USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents 22 CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" 23 ``` 24 25 ## Read and write scope 26 27 | Step | Read | Write | 28 |---|---|---| 29 | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_agents/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | 30 | 1 | `METADATA`, `TEMPLATE`, `PAPERS` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | 31 32 Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. 33 34 ## Steps 35 36 `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. 37 38 ```python 39 # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. 40 print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") 41 if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) 42 for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): 43 out = MD_OPT(stem(md)) 44 if exists(out) and out ends with ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") 51 print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: copied unchanged"); continue 52 print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") 53 for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once 54 raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers 55 append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches 56 print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") 57 append(out, "") 58 log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas 59 print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") 60 run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks 61 print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_skipped} skipped") 62 63 # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. 64 if any MD_RAW file has no finished MD_OPT file: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first 65 print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") 66 if not exists(RESULT): 67 write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only; do not copy example rows 68 write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) 69 log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run 70 read(METADATA); read(TEMPLATE, rows=2..6 + first 3 rows with PJP mths filled) # column rules + value format; TEMPLATE column order differs 71 for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): # LC_ALL=C order; one paper at a time: finish its LOG line before starting the next 72 if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run 73 print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue 74 started = now_utc() 75 remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by File_name); state count in LOG note 76 if broken(paper): # see Broken papers 77 append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) 78 print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue 79 print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") 80 for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once 81 append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch 82 print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") 83 if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data 84 append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) 85 print(f" no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue 86 log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems) 87 print(f" done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}") 88 check_paper(paper) 89 print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers") 90 run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}") # see Checks 91 print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed}") 92 ``` 93 94 Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. 95 96 Token usage: do not estimate tokens. Every log line ends with 6 empty `TOKEN_COLS` cells. After the session, `USAGE` fills them per paper from the session transcript, using the `started` and `finished` times, so record both for every paper. 97 98 ## Markdown optimisation 99 100 Compare each `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. `MD_RAW` holds scanned PDFs only; their raw text may be poor OCR or empty (no text layer): then build each page from the PDF page image. 101 102 - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. 103 - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. 104 - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. 105 - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). 106 - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. 107 - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. 108 109 ## Extraction rules 110 111 - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. 112 - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. 113 - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. 114 - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. 115 - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. 116 - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. 117 - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `Location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `Notes`. 118 - Site names: copy the name exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section. Do not add words (e.g. park or region name) and do not remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column `A`) to that name. Sites nested in larger sites: use the finest level with species data; a site named only by a code keeps the code (e.g. `E1`). Same site = same string on every row. 119 - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `Notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. 120 - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `Location_name` = those site names joined by `; `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites. 121 - Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry; `Notes` of each starts with `separate entry in paper` and names what differs. 122 - Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `Notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates). 123 - Measure defined as a percentage of a cohort or population flowering: 50% -> `Time to 50% flowering`, 80% -> `Time to 80% flowering`, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). 124 - `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` only for: maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed; or the primary-juvenile-period-in-months rule under Time columns. 125 - Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N`, e.g. `>4`. 126 - Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `Notes`. 127 - Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them. 128 - Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `Notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `Notes`. 129 - Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `Notes` only. 130 - Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `Notes`. 131 132 ## Broken papers and papers without data 133 134 Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. # Data extraction pipeline ## Setup ```python AGENTS = {"opus-5-5": "claude-opus-5-5", "sonnet-5-5": "claude-sonnet-5-5"} # slug: exact model ID; one session per agent slug = AGENTS key whose model ID is the model running this session # not in AGENTS: stop and tell the user MD_AGENT = "opus-5-5" # only this agent runs Step 0 RUN = "test" # "test" = trial run; "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT TEMPLATE = ROOT + "references/template.csv" # row 1 = header (29 columns); rows 2+ = worked examples; new columns = NA in examples METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example; ' | ' separates alternatives in allowed_values and example MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md/*.md" # pdf2md.py output for scanned PDFs only (text-layer PDFs go straight to md_agents/) PDF_DONE = "data/papers_test/pdf_done/*.pdf" # source PDF for each MD_RAW file; same file stem MD_OPT = "data/papers_test/md_agents/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md" # extraction input: MD_OPT files of scanned PDFs + raw pdf2md files of text-layer PDFs (end comment "md_opt: none"); pages split by RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (28 columns) LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" ``` ## Read and write scope | Step | Read | Write | |---|---|---| | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_agents/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | | 1 | `METADATA`, `TEMPLATE`, `PAPERS` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. ## Steps `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. ```python # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): out = MD_OPT(stem(md)) if exists(out) and out ends with ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: copied unchanged"); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") append(out, "") log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_skipped} skipped") # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. if any MD_RAW file has no finished MD_OPT file: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") if not exists(RESULT): write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only; do not copy example rows write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run read(METADATA); read(TEMPLATE, rows=2..6 + first 3 rows with PJP mths filled) # column rules + value format; TEMPLATE column order differs for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): # LC_ALL=C order; one paper at a time: finish its LOG line before starting the next if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue started = now_utc() remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by File_name); state count in LOG note if broken(paper): # see Broken papers append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f" no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems) print(f" done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}") check_paper(paper) print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers") run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}") # see Checks print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed}") ``` Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. Token usage: do not estimate tokens. Every log line ends with 6 empty `TOKEN_COLS` cells. After the session, `USAGE` fills them per paper from the session transcript, using the `started` and `finished` times, so record both for every paper. ## Markdown optimisation Compare each `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. `MD_RAW` holds scanned PDFs only; their raw text may be poor OCR or empty (no text layer): then build each page from the PDF page image. - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. ## Extraction rules - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `Location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `Notes`. - Site names: copy the name exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section. Do not add words (e.g. park or region name) and do not remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column `A`) to that name. Sites nested in larger sites: use the finest level with species data; a site named only by a code keeps the code (e.g. `E1`). Same site = same string on every row. - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `Notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `Location_name` = those site names joined by `; `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites. - Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry; `Notes` of each starts with `separate entry in paper` and names what differs. - Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `Notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates). - Measure defined as a percentage of a cohort or population flowering: 50% -> `Time to 50% flowering`, 80% -> `Time to 80% flowering`, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). - `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` only for: maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed; or the primary-juvenile-period-in-months rule under Time columns. - Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N`, e.g. `>4`. - Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `Notes`. - Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them. - Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `Notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `Notes`. - Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `Notes` only. - Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `Notes`. ## Broken papers and papers without data Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. Write an NA row when: - **broken**: file empty or under 1,000 bytes; no `

content.text:
`CLAUDE.md` is fine for token usage; its own length barely matters. The big costs are how a run is structured, and 2 places where the file contradicts itself or its inputs.

**Where the tokens go:** the last Opus run made 95 requests and read about 300k tokens of context per request, 29M in total. `CLAUDE.md` is about 4.7k of that 300k, about 1.6%. Most of the rest is earlier papers and tool output piling up in one session. Trimming the text would save under 0.5% per run, so trim only for clarity.

**Biggest saving: 1 subagent per paper.** The main session would loop over the papers. For each paper it would start a subagent on the same model with a short task: "extract `{paper}` per `CLAUDE.md` Step 1, append to `RESULT`, write the LOG line, run `check_paper`". Each subagent starts with only `CLAUDE.md`, `METADATA` and that one paper, about 30–80k tokens instead of about 300k.
- **Estimated saving:** about 4–6 times fewer tokens per run. That's an estimate; a test run would confirm it.
- **Accuracy:** it should improve, because a fresh context stops earlier papers leaking into later ones and avoids the long-context drift seen in Sonnet's out-of-order papers.
- **Token counting:** `usage.py` already reads subagent transcripts, so per-paper counts keep working if papers run one at a time.

**Accuracy and format problems in the file:**

content.text:
`TEMPLATE` is the older hand-built dataset (Harvey et al. 2017, 133 rows). Step 1 tells agents to read some of its rows "for value format", but those rows break the current format rules in almost every row. Since the main aim now is the same format from both models, it's a source of conflicting examples.

**How `TEMPLATE` conflicts with the current rules (133 example rows):**

| `TEMPLATE` example | Current rule (`METADATA` / `CLAUDE.md`) |
|---|---|
| `subsp` = `*` (18 rows) | Never `*`; status goes in `native_status` |
| `scientific_name` = `Avena sativa *`, trailing spaces (111 rows), `Banksia  verticillata` with a double space | Genus + ' ' + Species, trimmed |
| Leading or trailing spaces in `Genus`, `fire_response`, `Notes`, `Fire_severity` | Trim every cell |
| `Source` = `Harvey JM, Hopkins AJM, … (2017) … 339–347.` (133 rows) | APA style, ASCII hyphen, no en dash |
| `Notes`: "Fire severity supported by Vic Government Report…" with a URL | Paper only, no background knowledge; fixed `Notes` order |
| Column order differs, plus 2 unnamed columns | `COLUMNS` order, 28 columns |

The `CLAUDE.md` rules ("trim spaces; `TEMPLATE` has some", "never `*`") are there to undo `TEMPLATE`'s habits. Every run, the agent reads examples and then rules that override them, which is a source of format drift: the models resolve the conflict differently.

**What `TEMPLATE` still adds:**
- A worked example of the `PJP mths` and `_repr4` pair (`12` and `1`, `48` and `4`).
- Codes such as `O/r`.
- Range form `3.0-4.0`.

All 3 fit as `METADATA` examples; `METADATA` already holds most of them.

**Proposed change:**
1. Step 1 stops reading `TEMPLATE`: remove the `read(TEMPLATE, …)` call, the `TEMPLATE` line in the Setup block, and `TEMPLATE` in the Read and write scope table.
2. `METADATA` becomes the only format reference. Before removing `TEMPLATE`, I'd check its examples include the `PJP mths`/`_repr4` pair and an `O/r`-style code.
3. Columns section: keep "names match `TEMPLATE` exactly", because the meta-analysis joins on those names. Drop "omit the 2 unnamed `TEMPLATE` columns" and "new columns are NA in `TEMPLATE` examples".
4. The `TEMPLATE` file itself stays unchanged as your reference, and `log_session.py` still snapshots it.

**Effect:**
- **Format:** 1 source of examples instead of 2 that conflict.
- **Tokens:** about 2–3k saved per session, which is small.

Should I apply it?

`data/inference_test/references/metadata.csv` is the column dictionary for Step 1. It has 1 row per `RESULT` column, 28 rows in the same order as `COLUMNS` in `CLAUDE.md`, and it's now the only place column-specific rules live. It's about 9 KB, roughly 2.5k tokens, read once per Step 1 session.

**Fields:**

| Field | Content | Example (`fire_response categorical_surv1`) |
|---|---|---|
| `column` | Exact `RESULT` column name | `fire_response categorical_surv1` |
| `group` | Group, as in the `COLUMNS` comments | `fire response` |
| `type` | `text`, `categorical` or `numerical` | `categorical` |
| `unit` | Fixed unit, `Time_unit` (the paper's unit), or empty | (empty) |
| `allowed_values` | Allowed values separated by ` \| `; `as printed` = an open list | `obligate \| resprouter \| code as printed` |
| `trait_code` | Code in the Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database | `surv1` |
| `definition` | What the column measures | "Resprouting after full canopy scorch…" |
| `rule` | How to fill it: when, form, edge cases | `FRR` -> `resprouter`; remove spaces in codes… |
| `example` | Forms to copy, separated by ` \| ` | `obligate \| ?r \| K/r` |

**Who uses it:**
- **Step 1 agents** read it once at the start, as rules on the same footing as `CLAUDE.md`. When a rule leaves the form of a value open, `CLAUDE.md` says to use the form of the example.
- **`check.py`** doesn't read it. Its checks are written in the script, so a new rule added here needs a matching check added there by hand.
- **`log_session.py`** snapshots it with each run, so every run in `logs/runs/` records which rules it used.

**What it says, by group:**
- **Taxon:** name letters only, rank words standardised to `subsp.`, `var.` or `f.` and kept in `subsp`, `scientific_name` = Genus + Species, `native_status` in the paper's own term, `Family` with only the first letter capitalised.
- **Fire response:** mapping codes to `obligate` or `resprouter` (including `FRR`), copied codes with spaces removed, `resprouter_type` in lower case and singular, joined with `; `.
- **Time after fire:** which measure goes in which column, fixed units (months or years) vs the paper's unit in `Time_unit`, the `PJP mths` with `_repr4` pair.
- **Site:** `Location_name` as printed, with table codes mapped to names; finest site level; shared rows joined with `; `; coordinates to at most 4 decimals with no trailing zeros.
- **Fire:** type, season in calendar order, severity as printed when the paper uses a different scale.
- **Record:** the `Notes` item order and page-number style, `Source` in APA style with the DOI, `File_name` the same on every row.

**Upkeep:**
- **Edit it as CSV.** Rules contain commas and quotes, so edit with a CSV tool or `csv` in Python, not by hand.
- **2 copies.** `data/inference/references/metadata.csv` (for `RUN = "full"`) is still the old version. Copy the test version over before the full run.
- **Agents may not edit it** (the "Do not" list in `CLAUDE.md`). Only you, or I between runs, change it.

**Weak spots:**
- **Open lists:** `Fire_severity`, `Fire_type`, `resprouter_type` and copied fire-response codes allow values "as printed". That keeps the values accurate, but `hot` vs `High` style differences between models remain possible.
- **Long `Notes` rule:** the order is fixed, but the wording inside each item is free.

I'm assuming you mean spaces in the column names, such as `PJP mths`, `fire_response categorical_surv1` and `Time to 50% flowering`.

I'd keep the spaces during extraction and rename at the analysis stage.
- **Reason:** the column names match the existing dataset exactly, so both datasets combine directly. Renaming only the new results would break that match unless you also rename the existing dataset.
- **The current names also mix styles:** underscores, spaces, `%`, and mixed case (`Genus`, `PJP mths`). Underscores alone wouldn't make them tidy.

**Why underscores would be nicer:** no backticks or quotes in R or Python (`df$PJP_mths` instead of `` df$`PJP mths` ``), and fewer problems with tools that split names on spaces.

**Easiest route:** rename once, in R, for both datasets at the same point:
```r
library(janitor)
df <- clean_names(df)   # "Time to 50% flowering" -> time_to_50_percent_flowering
```
The same call on both datasets gives matching names with no changes to the pipeline.

**If you'd rather rename in the pipeline itself,** these all need changing together:
- `COLUMNS` in `CLAUDE.md`
- the `column` field of `metadata.csv`
- the column constants in `check.py` (e.g. `FIXED_YEARS`, `DUP_KEY`)
- the existing dataset, if you still want to join on it

**If you meant file names:** `1_pdf2md.py` already replaces spaces with `_` in new `.md` names. Only `Benson 1985 Cunninghamia_primary juvenile period.md` still has spaces, because it predates the change. I can rename it so all file names match.

I'd keep spaces in the cell data. Values with spaces cause no problem in R or Python; only column names need special syntax. Underscores in cells would also add a new rule for both models to apply the same way.

**Free text** (`scientific_name`, `Location_name`, `Notes`, `Source`, `resprouter_type` when copied as printed): keep the spaces.
- **Names:** `Acacia buxifolia` has to match taxonomic lists such as APC and the Fire Ecology Database exactly. `Acacia_buxifolia` would need converting back before any matching.
- **Accuracy:** values are copied as printed (`Bambra Road, Angahook-Lorne State Park`), and changing spaces would alter what the paper says.
- **Format:** the models would apply underscores to "as printed" values differently.

**Categories:** only `Fire_type` has multi-word allowed values (`prescribed burn`, `experimental burn`). Changing those to `prescribed_burn` is possible but gains little, since R reads `"prescribed burn"` fine.

**Column names:** spaces are the awkward part there, so rename them as in my last reply. `janitor::clean_names()` changes the names and leaves the cells alone.

**Separators:** `; ` between values in a cell stays either way. Underscores wouldn't replace it.

If you still want underscores in the categories, I'd limit it to the allowed values in `metadata.csv` (just `Fire_type`) and add a check for it.

e.g. `autumn; spring`
genus |  | As printed in the paper. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed as '?stenophylla'". | EX: Acacia
species |  | As printed in the paper. Epithet only; infraspecific rank and name (subsp., var., f.) go in subsp. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed  | EX: buxifolia
subsp | rank + name | Keep the rank word, written as subsp., var. or f. ('ssp.' or 'subsp' -> 'subsp.'; 'variety' -> 'var.'; 'forma' -> 'f.'); other ranks (e.g. nothosubsp.) as printed. Remove other marks printed with the name (e.g. '?'); printed form  | EX: subsp. buxifolia | var. lanceolatus | f. glauca
scientific_name |  | genus + ' ' + species. Never include the subspecies, variety or form, or '*'. | EX: Acacia buxifolia
native_status | native | introduced | exotic | naturalised | weed | as printed | Use the paper's term, in lower case: from a symbol or code defined in the paper (e.g. '*' = introduced; code 'Exotic'), a table column, or the text. Unmarked taxon -> 'native' only if the paper says unmarked taxa are native; other | EX: native | exotic
family |  | As printed, in lower case ('MYRTACEAE' or 'Myrtaceae' -> 'myrtaceae'). Empty if not stated. | EX: myrtaceae
fire_response_categorical_surv1 | obligate | resprouter | code as printed | Code defined in the paper as killed / fire-sensitive / obligate seeder -> obligate. Defined as resprouting, including facultative resprouters that also recruit from seed (e.g. FRR = facultative regrowth regenerator) -> resprouter. | EX: obligate | ?r | K/r
resprouter_type | as printed | As printed in the paper, but in lower case and singular ('rhizomes' -> 'rhizome'; 'lignotubers' -> 'lignotuber'). Several types joined by '; ', also when printed with 'and', 'or' or 'and/or' ('epicormic and/or basal' -> 'epicormic | EX: lignotuber | basal; lignotuber
pjp_mths |  | Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in months. Then also fill time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4 (months / 12). | EX: 18
primary_juvenile_period |  | Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in years. | EX: 3 | 3.0-4.0 | >8
age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3 |  | Time or age to first flowering from seed, when the paper uses other wording than 'primary juvenile period'. | EX: 2.5
secondary_juvenile_period |  | Fill only when the paper's term is 'secondary juvenile period'. Unit in time_unit. | EX: 1
time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a |  | Time to first flowering or reproduction of resprouts, when the paper uses other wording than 'secondary juvenile period'. | EX: 1.5
time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4 |  | Fill only for maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed, or from pjp_mths (months / 12, no notes entry). Time for 50% of individuals to flower goes to time_to_50_percent_flowering. | EX: 1.5
time_to_50_percent_flowering |  | As stated in the paper, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). Not maturation age. Unit in time_unit. | EX: 9.96
time_to_80_percent_flowering |  | Time after fire until 80% of individuals flower, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity). Unit in time_unit. | EX: 11.19

lines: - Precision: copy values with exactly the decimals printed in the paper. Do not round or add trailing zeros (`3.0` stays `3.0`; `3` stays `3`). Converted value: paper or source states the value in the target unit -> copy it as printed. Otherwise round to 3 decimals, drop trailing zeros (26 months -> 2.167; 30 months -> 2.5; 48 months -> 4).
- Ranges: `min-max`, no spaces (`3.0 - 16.0` -> `3.0-16.0`). Open bounds as printed (`>23`, `<2`). Uncertain value: no `?` in the cell; explain in `notes`.

-CSV format: UTF-8, comma separator, LF line endings, decimal point `.`. Quote any cell containing a comma, quote, or newline; double inner quotes. Empty cell = no value; `NA` only in NA rows. Trim leading and trailing spaces in every cell. Case: lower case in every cell (`Myrtaceae` -> `myrtaceae`, `Summer` -> `summer`, author and place names too), except: first letter of `genus` (also in `scientific_name`); `NA`; fire response codes copied as printed (case can carry meaning, e.g. `R` vs `r`); `file_name` (= file stem, also in `source` when used there). Several values in one cell: separate with `; ` (semicolon, space), e.g. `Autumn; Spring`; a `/` printed inside a single value (e.g. code `K/r`, a site name) stays as printed. Dashes: ASCII hyphen `-` in every cell, including names, codes and `source` (en dash `–` or em dash `—` -> `-`). Form not set by a rule: use the form of the `METADATA` example. Uncertain value: keep the format; explain in `notes`.

Column names are now lower case with `_` throughout, and every cell is lower case apart from genus and a few other exceptions. I made 2 exceptions you didn't ask for, both to avoid losing information; see "Kept their case" below. I tested `check.py` against the last Opus run converted to the new format, and it works.

**Column names:** `janitor::clean_names()` style, e.g.:
- `PJP mths` becomes `pjp_mths`
- `fire_response categorical_surv1` becomes `fire_response_categorical_surv1`
- `Time to 50% flowering_repr4` becomes `time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4`

Running `clean_names()` on the existing dataset in R gives the same 28 names, so the two still join.

**Cell values:** lower case in every cell (`myrtaceae`, `summer`, `high`, place names, `source` in APA style, `notes`), except:
- the first letter of `genus`, also in `scientific_name`;
- `NA`.

**Kept their case:**
- **Codes copied as printed, in any column including `notes`.** Case can carry meaning in these codes (`R` vs `r`, e.g. majority vs minority resprouting in the NSW database), so lower-casing them would lose data.
- **`file_name`**, also in `source` when it's used there: it must equal the file stem to match the LOG and the paper.

If you'd rather lower-case these too, it's a 1-line change.

**Files changed:**
- **`CLAUDE.md`:**
  - `COLUMNS` and all column references use the new names.
  - The Columns section explains the `clean_names()` naming.
  - A new Case rule sits in the CSV format paragraph.
- **`metadata.csv`:**
  - The `column` field and all name references in the rules use the new names.
  - `family`, seasons, severity, `location_name`, `notes` and `source` rules and examples are lower case.
  - Pages are written `pdf p. N` when no page number is printed.
- **`check.py`:**
  - It uses the new names.
  - Seasons are checked in lower case.
  - **Case errors:** any capital letters outside the exceptions.
  - **Case warnings (`notes` only):** quoted codes and printed forms may legitimately keep capitals there.
  - The `Family` capitalisation check is gone.

**Test:** I converted the last Opus run to the new names and lower case, keeping `notes` unchanged, then ran `check.py` on it.
- **2 errors:** the expected hash mismatches.
- **416 warnings on `notes`:** expected, because `notes` wasn't converted.
- **120 warnings on plural `resprouter_type`.**

I removed the temporary files afterwards.

**Still to do:**
- `data/inference/references/metadata.csv` (the full-run copy) is still the old version.
- `tests/ab_raw_md/compare.py` uses the old names; it's only needed if you keep the A/B test folder.
- Old run snapshots in `logs/runs/` keep the old names.

Nothing is committed.

Both models now produce the same format. Neither run has errors, and every remaining difference I found is a difference in values, not format.

| | opus | sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| Rows | 4403 | 4426 |
| Done | 19 | 20 |
| no_data | 2 | 1 |
| Broken | 0 | 0 |
| Errors | 0 | 0 |
| Tokens | 43.1M (2.05M per paper) | 28.4M (1.35M per paper) |

**Same format in both models:**
- **Lower case:** applied everywhere except genus, codes and `file_name`.
- **`family`:** e.g. `myrtaceae`.
- **Seasons and `resprouter_type`:** seasons as `summer` and `autumn; spring`; `resprouter_type` singular, joined with `; ` (`stem; lignotuber`, `sucker; basal`).
- **`fire_response`:** codes keep their printed case (`R s`, `pR`, `?K`), and `FRR` becomes `resprouter` in both.
- **`location_name`:** lower case, shared rows joined with `; `.
- **`source`:** APA style in lower case, with the DOI where printed, and the file stem for nswfrrd.
- **`notes`:** starts with the source location (`appendix 1, p. 151`, `table 5, p. 28`).

**Value differences, which are fine:**
- **Wark `location_name`:** Opus used the subsites (`e1`, `e1; e2`), Sonnet used `angahook-lorne state park` for every row. Sonnet broke the "finest level" rule here, but `check.py` can't detect that without reading the paper.
- **`fire_severity`:** Wark `severe` vs `high`; Benson empty vs `hot`; Ooi empty vs `very high`.
- **`source` details:** Ooi and Auld 2007 `(n.d.)` vs the year; Wahren `c-h.` vs `c.-h.`.
- **Row counts:** Ooi 5 vs 13, Wark 181 vs 200, bt9830293 no_data vs 3 rows.

**1 thing to fix: the `notes` case warning is noise.**
- It gives 3914 warnings for Opus and 4233 for Sonnet, and Opus's report is 697 KB.
- Almost all are legitimate: codes (`R`, `S`, `pK`, `FRR`), genus names (`Grevillea`, `Eucalyptus`), or quoted printed words (`Exotic`, `Mortality`).
- A warning that is nearly always a false alarm wastes the agents' time; Opus may have spent tokens reviewing it.
- **Suggestion:** remove that warning from `check.py`. The case errors for every other column stay.

**Tokens rose** compared with the last round, mainly because Kubiak and nswfrrd (about 4000 rows) are extracted now instead of marked broken. Opus also had a 42-minute pause in the middle of Auld 2007, probably a rate limit. The subagent-per-paper change is still the biggest available saving.

Should I remove the `notes` warning from `check.py`?

I agree. A wrong format can be fixed by a script in seconds, but a wrong value means going back to the paper. So far we've only measured format, and we haven't measured accuracy at all. I've updated my notes to put accuracy first, format second.

**Accuracy can be measured now.** The hand-extracted reference in `data/reference/` (1158 rows) covers most of the test papers:

| Paper | Reference rows |
|---|---|
| Kubiak | 635 |
| Wark | 163 |
| Burrows | 57 |
| Benson | 40 |
| Knox | 18 |
| Enright | 14 |
| Miller | 9 |
| Muir, Auld | 8 each |
| Wahren, Denham, Bradstock, Pyke, Zammit, Morgan, Ashton | 1–4 each |
| Ooi | 0 |

Agents never read this folder; I would only use it to score their results.

**Proposed next steps:**
1. **Accuracy score:** a script compares each model's results with the reference, paper by paper.
   - **Taxa:** how many reference taxa each model found, how many it missed, and how many extra taxa it added.
   - **Values:** for taxa found in both, agreement on fire response and each time column (exact match, then close match such as `3` vs `3.0` or a range vs its midpoint).
   - **Disagreements:** listed per cell with the source location from `notes`, so the reference itself can be checked.

   This shows which rules cause wrong values, which is where rule changes pay off most.
2. **Both models in agreement vs disagreement:** count cells where both models give the same value and test whether those are more often right. If they are, disagreement between the models can be the flag for which rows you check by hand.
3. **Format in post-processing:** move deterministic fixes (lower case, trimming, dashes, season order, trailing zeros, separators) into a script run after extraction. Agents then spend their attention on values, and `CLAUDE.md` can drop some format rules. That cuts tokens and the rules competing for attention.

content.text:
Yes, F1, but report precision and recall next to it, because for a meta-analysis the two kinds of error cost different amounts. Score at 2 levels: whether the right records are found, and whether their values are right.

**Level 1: records (are the right species found?)**
- **Match key:** paper + taxon (`scientific_name` + `subsp`), after normalising case and spaces.
- **TP:** a reference taxon the model found. **FN:** a reference taxon it missed. **FP:** a taxon it added that isn't in the reference.
- **Site:** not part of the key, because humans and models name sites differently. Site agreement is scored as a value instead.

**Level 2: values (are the extracted values right?)** Each cell of a matched record falls in 1 of 5 cases:

| Reference | Model | Counts as |
|---|---|---|
| value | same value | TP |
| value | different value | FP and FN (a wrong value) |
| value | empty | FN (missed) |
| empty | value | FP (extra, or an omission in the reference) |
| empty | empty | not counted |

- **Scored columns:** fire response, resprouter type, the 10 time columns, time unit, coordinates, rainfall, fire type, season, severity, native status. Not `notes` or `source`.
- **Normalised before comparing:** `3` = `3.0`; ranges compared bound by bound; `>8` is exact; categories lower case and trimmed.

**Which number leads:**
- **Precision** = the share of filled cells that are right. This is your main concern: wrong information is the costly error.
- **Recall** = the share of reference values found. A missing value is cheaper to fix: you just look it up.
- **F1** is a fair single summary. **F0.5** weights precision twice as much as recall, which matches what you said about wrong values. I'd lead with F0.5 and always show P and R too.

**Logging, compatible with `sessions.csv`:**
- `data/inference_test/logs/benchmark.csv`, long format with 1 row per run × model × paper × level × column.
- **Columns:** `session_id, step, slug, date, git, claude_md_sha256, metadata_sha256, paper, level, column, tp, fp, fn, precision, recall, f1, f05`.
- **Store the counts** (TP/FP/FN), not just the scores. Totals per run, paper or column can then be recomputed correctly by summing counts before dividing (micro-averaging).
- **Joins on `session_id` + `step`** with `sessions.csv`, which gives accuracy against tokens for each rule version.
- **`benchmark_details.csv`:** 1 line per wrong, missed or extra cell, with the model's source location from `notes`, so you can check quickly whether the model or the reference is wrong.

**Past runs:** the snapshots in `logs/runs/` can all be scored by mapping old column names to new ones. That shows whether the rule changes so far improved accuracy or only format.

**Files:**
- `scripts/claude/benchmark.py`, run by you after each session. It could also run from the end-of-session hook.
- A guard line in `CLAUDE.md`: never read `data/papers_test/answers/`.

Go ahead with this design, F0.5 as the headline and past runs scored too?

def log_step(path, session, step, since, until, slug, models, version):
    start = usage.parse_time(since).astimezone()

    # 1-2. transcript and output snapshot
    run_dir = LOGS / "runs" / f"{step}_{slug}_{session}"
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(path, run_dir / "transcript.jsonl")
    for f in (REPO / "CLAUDE.md", REPO / "scripts/claude/check.py", ROOT / "references/template.csv", ROOT / "references/metadata.csv"):
        if not (run_dir / f.name).exists():  # first logging of the session = closest to the run
            shutil.copy2(f, run_dir / f.name)

    # 3. sessions.csv line, one per session and step
    sessions = LOGS / "sessions.csv"
    if not sessions.exists():
        with open(sessions, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n").writerow(SESSIONS_HEADER + usage.USAGE_COLS)
    if not any((r["session_id"], r["step"]) == (session, step) for r in csv.DictReader(open(sessions, encoding="utf-8", newline=""))):
        header = next(csv.reader(open(sessions, encoding="utf-8", newline="")))
        row = dict(zip(SESSIONS_HEADER, [start.strftime("%Y-%m-%d_%H%M"), step, slug, "|".join(models), version, session]))
        with open(sessions, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=header, restval="", lineterminator="\n").writerow(row)

    # 4. token columns (only for a known agent, whose log the step wrote), counting only this step's part of the session
    if slug in AGENTS.values():
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(Path(usage.__file__)), "--step", step, "--slug", slug,
                        "--session", str(path), "--window", f"{since},{until or ''}"], check=False)

    outputs = ([LOGS / "md_opt_log.csv", LOGS / "md_opt_check.csv"] if step == "step0" else
               [ROOT / f"results/{slug}.csv", LOGS / f"{slug}_log.csv", LOGS / f"{slug}_check.csv"])
    for f in outputs:
        if f.exists():
            shutil.copy2(f, run_dir / f.name)
    print(f"logged {step} | {slug} | session {session} | {run_dir.relative_to(REPO)}", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Score Step 1 results against the human-extracted answers (accuracy benchmark).

Usage (from the repo root):
    python scripts/claude/benchmark.py              # score every Step 1 snapshot in logs/runs/ not yet in benchmark.csv
    python scripts/claude/benchmark.py --rescore    # score all snapshots again
    python scripts/claude/benchmark.py --run <dir>  # score one snapshot folder

Ground truth: data/papers_test/answers/Juvenile period data.csv (agents never read it).
Answer rows are matched to papers by the start of their Source; papers without answer rows are not scored.
Only papers extracted in the run itself are scored (LOG started >= the run's last _run line), so papers
carried over from an earlier run are not counted twice.

Two levels, each with true positives (tp), false positives (fp) and false negatives (fn):
  record: taxa (genus + species + subsp) per paper. tp = taxon in both; fp = model only; fn = answers only.
  value:  for each taxon in both, the set of values of a column over the taxon's rows.
          tp = values in both; fp = model values not in the answers (wrong or extra); fn = answer values the model lacks.
Scores: precision, recall, f1, and f05 (F0.5: precision weighted twice as much as recall; headline score).

Writes, under data/inference_test/logs/:
  benchmark.csv          1 line per run x paper x level x column, plus totals (paper "_all", column "_all");
                         joins sessions.csv on (session_id, step)
  benchmark_details.csv  1 line per taxon or value in only one side, with the model's source location from notes
"""

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import re
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
LOGS = REPO / "data/inference_test/logs"
RUNS = LOGS / "runs"
ANSWERS = REPO / "data/papers_test/answers/Juvenile period data.csv"
OUT = LOGS / "benchmark.csv"
DETAILS = LOGS / "benchmark_details.csv"

# start of the answer Source -> start of the paper's file stem (spaces as "_")
PAPERS = [
    ("Kubiak PJ. (2009)", "Kubiak_Cunn_2009"),
    ("Wark, M.C. (1997)", "biostor-259750"),
    ("Burrows, N. D., Wardell-Johnson", "Post_fire_juvenile_period_of_plants_in_s"),
    ("Benson, D. (1985)", "Benson_1985_Cunninghamia"),
    ("Miller, R.G., Enright", "Austral_Ecology_-_2025_-_Miller"),
    ("Muir AM", "Muir_et_al_2014"),
    ("Wahren, C.-H.A.", "Austral_Ecology_-_2002_-_Wahren"),
    ("Auld, T.D. & Scott, J. (1997)", "AuldScottProcFireEffectsIAWF1997"),
    ("Enright N.J. & Agne M.C. (2025)", "wf24046"),
    ("Enright, N.J., Marsula", "Journal_of_Ecology_-_2002_-_Enright"),
    ("Enright, N. J., Lamont, B. B., & Marsula", "enright1996"),
    ("Pyke, G.H. (1983)", "bt9830293"),
    ("Bradstock, R.A. & O'Connell", "Australian_Journal_of_Ecology_-_December_1988_-_BRADSTOCK"),
    ("Zammit & Westoby (1987)", "BF00040753"),
    ("Ashton, D.H. & Chappill", "bt9890001"),
    ("Denham, A.J. & Auld, T.D. (2002)", "bt02009"),
    ("Morgan, J.W & Lunt", "1-s2.0-S0006320798001128-main"),
    ("Auld, Tony D, Andrew J Denham", "J_Vegetation_Science_-_2007_-_Auld"),
    ("Knox K.J.E. & Clarke P.J. (2004)", "Knox_&_Clarke_2004"),
]

# answer column (old name) -> result column (new name); scored at the value level
VALUE_COLS = {
    "PJP mths": "pjp_mths",
    "Time to 50% flowering_repr4": "time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4",
    "Age at first flower production from seed_repr3": "age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3",
    "Time to first flower production resprout_repr3a": "time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a",
    "primary_juvenile_period": "primary_juvenile_period",
    "secondary_juvenile_period": "secondary_juvenile_period",
    "fire_response categorical_surv1": "fire_response_categorical_surv1",
    "resprouter_type": "resprouter_type",
    "Latitude": "latitude",
    "Longitude": "longitude",
    "Rainfall_mm": "rainfall_mm",
    "Fire_season_categorical": "fire_season_categorical",
    "Fire_severity_categorical": "fire_severity_categorical",
}
NUMERIC = {"pjp_mths", "time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4", "age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3",
           "time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a", "primary_juvenile_period", "secondary_juvenile_period",
           "rainfall_mm"}
COORDS = {"latitude", "longitude"}
INTRODUCED = {"introduced", "exotic", "naturalised", "naturalized", "weed"}

HEADER = ["session_id", "step", "slug", "date", "git", "claude_md_sha256", "metadata_sha256",
          "paper", "level", "column", "tp", "fp", "fn", "precision", "recall", "f1", "f05"]
DETAIL_HEADER = ["session_id", "slug", "paper", "taxon", "column", "kind", "model_value", "answer_value", "model_source_location"]

RANK_RE = re.compile(r"\b(subsp|ssp|var|f|forma|nothosubsp)\.?\s+", re.I)


def stem_key(stem):
    return stem.replace(" ", "_")


def paper_of_source(source):
    s = source.strip()
    return next((p for prefix, p in PAPERS if s.startswith(prefix)), None)


def paper_of_stem(stem):
    k = stem_key(stem)
    return next((p for _, p in PAPERS if k.startswith(p)), None)


def taxon(genus, species, subsp):
    clean = lambda s: re.sub(r"[?*()]", "", s).strip().lower()  # noqa: E731
    sub = clean(RANK_RE.sub("", subsp)) if subsp.strip() not in ("*", "NA") else ""
    return (clean(genus), clean(species), sub)


def number(s):
    s = s.strip().lstrip("~").replace("c.", "").strip()
    try:
        return f"{float(s):g}"
    except ValueError:
        return None


def norm(col, value):
    """Normalised values of a cell (a set: one cell can hold several values)."""
    v = value.strip().replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
    if not v or v == "NA":
        return set()
    if col in COORDS:
        n = number(v)
        return {f"{float(n):.2f}"} if n else {v.lower()}
    if col in NUMERIC:
        v = re.sub(r"\s*-\s*", "-", v)
        m = re.fullmatch(r"([<>]?)\s*([\d.]+)(?:-([\d.]+))?", v)
        if m:
            lo, hi = number(m.group(2)), number(m.group(3)) if m.group(3) else None
            if lo is not None:
                return {m.group(1) + lo + (f"-{hi}" if hi else "")}
        return {v.lower()}
    if col == "fire_response_categorical_surv1":
        return {v.lower() if v.lower() in ("obligate", "resprouter") else v.replace(" ", "")}
    parts = [p.strip().lower() for p in re.split(r"[;/,]| and | or ", v) if p.strip()]
    if col == "resprouter_type":
        parts = [re.sub(r"(?<=[a-rt-z])s$", "", p) for p in parts]  # rhizomes -> rhizome
    return {"; ".join(sorted(parts))} if col == "fire_season_categorical" else set(parts)


def scores(tp, fp, fn):
    p = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else ""
    r = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else ""
    f = lambda b: (1 + b * b) * p * r / (b * b * p + r) if p != "" and r != "" and (p or r) else ""  # noqa: E731
    return [round(x, 4) if x != "" else "" for x in (p, r, f(1), f(0.5))]


def load_answers():
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(ANSWERS, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="")))
    out = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set)))  # paper -> taxon -> column -> values
    for r in rows:
        paper = paper_of_source(r.get("Source", ""))
        if not paper or not r.get("Genus", "").strip():
            continue
        t = taxon(r["Genus"], r["Species"], r.get("subsp", ""))
        cell = out[paper][t]
        cell["_present"].add("1")
        for a, c in VALUE_COLS.items():
            cell[c] |= norm(c, r.get(a, ""))
        if "*" in r.get("subsp", "") + r.get("scientific_name", ""):
            cell["introduced"].add("introduced")
    return out


def load_run(run_dir):
    slug = run_dir.name.split("_")[1]
    session = run_dir.name.split("_", 2)[2]
    result, log = run_dir / f"{slug}.csv", run_dir / f"{slug}_log.csv"
    if not result.exists() or not log.exists():
        return None
    log_rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(log, encoding="utf-8", newline="")))
    runs = [r for r in log_rows if r["paper"] == "_run"]
    if not runs:
        return None
    start = runs[-1]["started"]
    fresh = {stem_key(r["paper"]) for r in log_rows if r["paper"] != "_run" and r["started"] >= start}
    note = runs[-1]["note"]
    meta = run_dir / "metadata.csv"
    info = {
        "session_id": session, "step": "step1", "slug": slug, "date": start[:10],
        "git": (re.search(r"git=([0-9a-f]+)", note) or [None, ""])[1],
        "claude_md_sha256": (re.search(r"claude_md_sha256=([0-9a-f]+)", note) or [None, ""])[1],
        "metadata_sha256": hashlib.sha256(meta.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if meta.exists() else "",
    }
    out = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set)))
    where = defaultdict(dict)
    for r in csv.DictReader(open(result, encoding="utf-8", newline="")):
        r = {k.strip(): v for k, v in r.items() if k}
        g = lambda *names: next((r[n] for n in names if n in r), "")  # noqa: E731  old or new column name
        stem = stem_key(g("file_name", "File_name"))
        paper = paper_of_stem(stem)
        if not paper or stem not in fresh or g("genus", "Genus") in ("NA", ""):
            continue
        t = taxon(g("genus", "Genus"), g("species", "Species"), g("subsp"))
        cell = out[paper][t]
        cell["_present"].add("1")
        for a, c in VALUE_COLS.items():
            cell[c] |= norm(c, g(c, a))
        if g("native_status").strip().lower() in INTRODUCED or "*" in g("subsp") + g("scientific_name"):
            cell["introduced"].add("introduced")
        where[paper].setdefault(t, g("notes", "Notes").split(";")[0].strip()[:80])
    return info, out, where, {paper_of_stem(s) for s in fresh} - {None}


def score_run(info, model, where, papers, answers):
    lines, details = [], []
    totals = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])
    cols = list(VALUE_COLS.values()) + ["introduced"]
    for paper in sorted(p for p in papers if p in answers):
        ans, mod = answers[paper], model.get(paper, {})
        a_t, m_t = set(ans), set(mod)
        rec = [len(a_t & m_t), len(m_t - a_t), len(a_t - m_t)]
        lines.append([paper, "record", "taxon", *rec])
        for k in range(3):
            totals[("record", "taxon")][k] += rec[k]
        for t in sorted(m_t - a_t):
            details.append([paper, " ".join(x for x in t if x), "taxon", "extra", "", "", where[paper].get(t, "")])
        for t in sorted(a_t - m_t):
            details.append([paper, " ".join(x for x in t if x), "taxon", "missed", "", "", ""])
        for col in cols:
            c = [0, 0, 0]
            for t in sorted(a_t & m_t):
                av, mv = ans[t][col], mod[t][col]
                c[0] += len(av & mv)
                c[1] += len(mv - av)
                c[2] += len(av - mv)
                if av != mv:
                    kind = "wrong" if av and mv else ("extra" if mv else "missed")
                    details.append([paper, " ".join(x for x in t if x), col, kind,
                                    "; ".join(sorted(mv)), "; ".join(sorted(av)), where[paper].get(t, "")])
            if any(c):
                lines.append([paper, "value", col, *c])
                for key in ((col,), ("_all",)):
                    for k in range(3):
                        totals[("value",) + key][k] += c[k]
    for (level, col), c in totals.items():
        lines.append(["_all", level, col, *c])
    base = [info[k] for k in HEADER[:7]]
    rows = [base + line + scores(*line[3:6]) for line in lines]
    return rows, [[info["session_id"], info["slug"], *d] for d in details]


def write(path, header, rows, drop_sessions):
    old = []
    if path.exists():
        old = [r for r in csv.reader(open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline=""))][1:]
        old = [r for r in old if r[0] not in drop_sessions]
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerows(old + rows)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--rescore", action="store_true", help="score all snapshots again")
    parser.add_argument("--run", help="score only this snapshot folder (name or path)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    answers = load_answers()
    done = set()
    if OUT.exists() and not args.rescore:
        done = {r["session_id"] for r in csv.DictReader(open(OUT, encoding="utf-8", newline=""))}
    dirs = [RUNS / Path(args.run).name] if args.run else sorted(RUNS.glob("step1_*"))
    all_rows, all_details, scored = [], [], set()
    for d in dirs:
        session = d.name.split("_", 2)[2]
        if session in done and not args.run:
            continue
        loaded = load_run(d)
        if not loaded:
            continue
        info, model, where, papers = loaded
        rows, details = score_run(info, model, where, papers, answers)
        if not rows:
            print(f"skip {d.name}: no scored papers (none extracted in this run, or none with answers)")
            continue
        all_rows += rows
        all_details += details
        scored.add(session)
        tot = {(r[8], r[9]): r for r in rows if r[7] == "_all"}
        rec, val = tot.get(("record", "taxon")), tot.get(("value", "_all"))
        n = len({r[7] for r in rows} - {"_all"})
        print(f"{info['date']} {info['slug']:10} {session[:8]} | papers {n:2} | taxa P {rec[13]} R {rec[14]} F0.5 {rec[16]}"
              + (f" | values P {val[13]} R {val[14]} F0.5 {val[16]}" if val else ""))
    if scored:
        write(OUT, HEADER, all_rows, scored)
        write(DETAILS, DETAIL_HEADER, all_details, scored)
        print(f"written: {OUT.relative_to(REPO)}, {DETAILS.relative_to(REPO)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    args = parser.parse_args()

    answers = load_answers()
    done = set()
    if OUT.exists() and not args.rescore:
        done = {r["session_id"] for r in csv.DictReader(open(OUT, encoding="utf-8", newline=""))}
    dirs = [RUNS / Path(args.run).name] if args.run else sorted(RUNS.glob("step1_*"))
    all_rows, all_details, scored = [], [], set()
    for d in dirs:
        session = d.name.split("_", 2)[2]
        if session in done and not args.run:
            continue
        loaded = load_run(d)
        if not loaded:
            continue
        info, model, where, papers = loaded
        rows, details = score_run(info, model, where, papers, answers)
        if not rows:
            print(f"skip {d.name}: no scored papers (none extracted in this run, or none with answers)")
            continue
        all_rows += rows
        all_details += details
        scored.add(session)
        tot = {(r[8], r[9]): r for r in rows if r[7] == "_all"}
        rec, val = tot.get(("record", "taxon")), tot.get(("value", "_all"))
        n = len({r[7] for r in rows} - {"_all"})
        print(f"{info['date']} {info['slug']:10} {session[:8]} | papers {n:2} | taxa P {rec[13]} R {rec[14]} F0.5 {rec[16]}"
              + (f" | values P {val[13]} R {val[14]} F0.5 {val[16]}" if val else ""))
    if scored:
        write(OUT, HEADER, all_rows, scored)
        write(DETAILS, DETAIL_HEADER, all_details, scored)
        print(f"written: {OUT.relative_to(REPO)}, {DETAILS.relative_to(REPO)}")

content.text:
The benchmark is built, and all past runs are scored. The main finding: on the same 4 papers, accuracy hasn't improved since the first runs on 10-02. The format rules added since then cost a little, mostly in fire response.

**Built:**
- **`scripts/claude/benchmark.py`:** scores each run against `data/papers_test/answers/`, with taxa as records and cells as values. It reports TP/FP/FN, precision, recall, F1 and F0.5.
- **Matching tolerances:**
  - rounding is allowed, so `2.596` matches `2.6`;
  - range bounds are compared, so rainfall `698-843` matches `698; 843`;
  - `secondary_juvenile_period` is converted to years using `time_unit`;
  - typos in names count as the same taxon (`poa sieheriana` = `poa sieberiana`, edit distance up to 2).
- **Encoding:** the answers file is saved by Excel (cp1252, not UTF-8), and the script reads it that way.
- **`data/inference_test/logs/benchmark.csv`:** 1 line per run × paper × level × column, with counts, so totals can be recomputed. It joins `sessions.csv` on `session_id` + `step`.
- **`benchmark_details.csv`:** every miss, extra, wrong value and name typo, with the model's source location.
- **Hook:** the end-of-session hook now runs the benchmark after each Step 1, so every new run is scored automatically.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** agents must not read `data/papers_test/answers/` or `logs/benchmark*.csv`.
- **Past runs:** 21 scored. Stray session `277cfa7d` is excluded: its snapshot holds a copy of `79bf9038`.

**Latest runs (19 papers with answers):**

| | Taxa P / R / F0.5 | Values P / R / F0.5 |
|---|---|---|
| opus `8cc94ea8` | 0.75 / 0.90 / 0.78 | 0.82 / 0.63 / 0.77 |
| sonnet `65379324` | 0.74 / 0.90 / 0.77 | 0.87 / 0.77 / 0.85 |

Taxa precision is low mainly because the models extract more taxa than the reference has; Kubiak alone has 200 extras. The reference may simply have skipped species, so it's worth looking at whether those extras are real.

**Same 4 papers across time (Benson, Knox, Kubiak, Muir), values F0.5:**

| Date | Values F0.5 |
|---|---|
| 10-02 (first runs) | 0.93–0.94 |
| 10-06 to 10-07 | 0.89–0.91 |
| 10-08, latest Sonnet | 0.90 |
| 10-08, latest Opus | 0.85 |

**Causes:**
1. **Fire response in Kubiak, about 170 cells:** the paper prints probable or uncertain codes (`pK`, `pR`, `?K`). The answers map them to `obligate` or `resprouter`, but since 10-06 the rules say to copy uncertain codes as printed. This is a rule decision you need to make.
2. **Opus left `fire_severity` empty for Kubiak:** 568 cells, while the answers have `high`. Opus also wrote `severe` instead of `high` for Wark.
3. **Opus `pjp_mths` for Burrows:** missed (0 of 30); Sonnet got 20.
4. **Gaps in the answers themselves:**
   - the answers keep codes like `O/r` where the rules map codes to words;
   - rainfall is missing for Wark (150 "extra" values);
   - some severity values come from outside the paper.

**Decision needed:** in `fire_response`, should probable codes (`pK` = probably killed, `pR` = probably resprouts) map to `obligate`/`resprouter`, with the code noted in `notes`, as the answers do?

Nothing is committed.

content.text:
Yes, a few, but the effect is small. Most of the "wrong" cells are differences in convention between your answers and the current rules, not formatting. In the 2 latest runs, 1025 cells count as wrong, and they fall into 3 groups:

**1. Scoring artefacts: the same information written differently, counted wrongly.** About 40 cells; I can fix these in the scorer.

| Model | Answer | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| `4; 5` (1 value per site row) | `4-5` (1 range) | different granularity |
| `3-4` | `3.0,4.0` | comma used as a range |
| `1.654` | `1.6` | the answer is truncated, not rounded, so my ±0.05 tolerance misses it |

**Fix:** a range matches a set of values with the same lowest and highest value; comma lists are read as ranges; tolerance becomes 1 unit of the answer's last decimal.

**2. Conventions: the rules and the answers handle the same paper differently.** About 600 cells, most of the total; a decision for you, not a formatting problem.

| Model (current rules) | Answer | Cells |
|---|---|---|
| `pK`, `pR`, `?K` (uncertain codes copied as printed) | `obligate`, `resprouter` | about 350 |
| `obligate` / `resprouter` (codes mapped to words) | `O/r`, `R/o`, `O/R` (codes kept) | about 190 |
| `severe` (as printed) | `high` | 151 |
| `tuberoid` | `tuber` | 40 |

The answers are mixed. They map probable codes (`pK`, `pR`) to words but keep 2-letter codes like `O/r`. These cells score low because the rules and the answers disagree, not because the model read the paper wrongly.

**Options:**
- **(a)** Change the rules to follow your answers' conventions.
- **(b)** Treat the answers' conventions as out of date and update the answers.
- **(c)** Report 2 scores: strict, and lenient with a mapping table (`pK` = `obligate`, `severe` = `high`, …).

My suggestion is (a) where the answers reflect what you want for the meta-analysis, and (c) meanwhile, so the score shows real reading errors.

**3. Real differences in values:** for example, `autumn; spring` vs `autumn` in Knox, extra rainfall values, latitude `-29.50` vs `-29.42`, and resprouter types. These are what the benchmark should catch, and they stay counted.

Should I fix group 1 in the scorer now? And for group 2, which conventions are right: those in your answers, or those in the current rules?

content.text:
The `?` marks in the results are real, not encoding errors. Every one comes from a paper that prints `?` to mean "possibly" or "uncertain", and the current rules copy it on purpose.

**Where they appear:**
- **`fire_response`, 79 cells in each model:** uncertain codes copied as printed, as `metadata.csv` says: "copy exactly as printed, including '?'". These are Kubiak `?K` (47), `?R` (9), `?r`, `?K/r`, and Benson `?fs` (17).
- **`notes`:**
  - **Code definitions repeated on every row of the paper:** "p = probably, ? = possibly" on all 1305 Kubiak rows (Sonnet), and "? = probably fire-sensitive" on 65 Benson rows. This makes up most of the 1380 Sonnet rows and 160 Opus rows.
  - **Printed forms quoted:** e.g. `code printed '?K'`, `printed 'F2?'`, `'?63w?'`, which record that the paper marked a value as uncertain.
- **`benchmark_details.csv`:** the same codes, plus 36 answer values that have `?` in your own answers file (e.g. `3.0-4.0?`).

**No encoding damage:** none of the files contains the Unicode replacement character. But 658 cells have non-ASCII characters, such as `°` in coordinates within `notes` and `‐` (U+2010) in some file names. If a viewer opens the CSV as something other than UTF-8, those can show up as `?`. In Excel, import as UTF-8 (Data > From Text/CSV > File origin 65001 UTF-8).

**This ties in with the code decision from my last message:**
- **Keep as now:** uncertain codes stay in `fire_response` with their `?`. Faithful to the paper, but harder to analyse, and it disagrees with your answers.
- **Map them:** `?K` and `pK` become `obligate`, `?R` and `pR` become `resprouter`, and the printed code moves to `notes`, e.g. `fire response code printed '?K' (possibly killed)`. This matches your answers, keeps `fire_response` to 2 values plus truly undefined codes, and the uncertainty stays traceable in `notes`.

My suggestion is to map them. Should I change the rule?
